answer: One-Time Challenge Grove. Each identity must solve a fresh, randomly generated puzzle whose solution seeds a unique state in a shared grove of puzzle instances; duplicates are rejected at submission. As the registration tide rises, puzzle difficulty scales with the current solver count, so mass creation slows sharply. At each dawn the grove rotates, invalidating stale solutions. An attacker pays escalating compute per identity plus continuous re-solving, making large sybil sets economically impractical.
